principles.name: Time Blocking
principles.description: Assigning every task or category of work to a dedicated, fixed block of time on the calendar, leaving no unscheduled gaps.
principles.mechanism: Treating time as a scarce, pre-committed resource reduces decision fatigue, prevents task-switching, and protects high-value cognitive work from reactive interruptions.
principles.source: Newport, C. (2016). Deep Work: Rules for Focused Success in a Distracted World. Grand Central Publishing.
principles.example: Block 9:00–11:00 AM each weekday in your calendar as 'Deep Work — no meetings', and use that window exclusively for the most cognitively demanding task of the day.

principles.name: Implementation Intention
principles.description: Forming a specific when–where–how plan for a desired behaviour using the format 'When situation X occurs, I will perform response Y'.
principles.mechanism: Pre-deciding the exact context bridges the intention–action gap by creating a mental link between a situational cue and the intended response, reducing deliberation at the moment of action.
principles.source: Gollwitzer, P. M. (1999). Implementation intentions: Strong effects of simple plans. American Psychologist, 54(7), 493–503.
principles.example: When I sit down at my desk each morning and open my laptop, I will write the three most important tasks for the day before opening email or Slack.

principles.name: If–Then Planning
principles.description: Creating specific contingency plans that link anticipated obstacles or triggers to pre-chosen productive responses.
principles.mechanism: Specifying an obstacle–response pair in advance reduces cognitive load when the obstacle occurs, because the required action has already been decided and encoded as a strong situational association.
principles.source: Gollwitzer, P. M., & Sheeran, P. (2006). Implementation intentions and goal achievement: A meta-analysis of effects and processes. Advances in Experimental Social Psychology, 38, 69–119.
principles.example: If I feel the urge to check social media during a focus block, then I will immediately write the next sentence of the document I am working on.

principles.name: Minimum Viable Progress
principles.description: Defining the smallest meaningful unit of forward movement on a task so that even a constrained day yields a sense of accomplishment.
principles.mechanism: Small wins activate positive affect and reinforce intrinsic motivation through the Progress Principle: perceptions of daily progress are the strongest predictor of inner work-life quality, sustaining engagement over time.
principles.source: Amabile, T., & Kramer, S. (2011). The Progress Principle: Using Small Wins to Ignite Joy, Engagement, and Creativity at Work. Harvard Business Review Press.
principles.example: Commit to writing just one paragraph of a report when time is scarce — completing that unit creates momentum and satisfaction rather than zero progress.

principles.name: Cognitive Offloading
principles.description: Externalising information — tasks, ideas, deadlines — into a trusted external system so that working memory is freed for active processing.
principles.mechanism: Working memory is severely capacity-limited; offloading cognitive content to an external medium reduces mental load, lowers anxiety caused by open loops, and enables deeper focus on the current task.
principles.source: Risko, E. F., & Gilbert, S. J. (2016). Cognitive offloading. Trends in Cognitive Sciences, 20(9), 676–688.
principles.example: Capture every incoming task, idea, and commitment into a single trusted inbox (e.g., a dedicated app) the moment it arises, then process that inbox once daily.

principles.name: Reward Substitution
principles.description: Replacing reliance on external rewards (money, praise) with the cultivation of intrinsic satisfaction derived from competence, autonomy, and purpose.
principles.mechanism: Self-determination theory shows that autonomous motivation — driven by genuine interest and personal values — produces greater persistence, creativity, and wellbeing than controlled motivation driven by external contingencies.
principles.source: Deci, E. L., & Ryan, R. M. (1985). Intrinsic Motivation and Self-Determination in Human Behavior. Plenum Press.
principles.example: Reframe a tedious weekly reporting task as an opportunity to improve your data analysis skill rather than focusing on the obligation to a manager.

principles.name: Environment Design
principles.description: Restructuring the physical or digital workspace to make productive behaviours the path of least resistance and unproductive behaviours harder to access.
principles.mechanism: Environmental cues automatically trigger associated behaviours; reducing friction for desired actions and increasing friction for competing actions shifts default behaviour without requiring willpower.
principles.source: Thaler, R. H., & Sunstein, C. R. (2008). Nudge: Improving Decisions about Health, Wealth, and Happiness. Yale University Press. (See also Fogg, B. J. (2020). Tiny Habits. Houghton Mifflin Harcourt.)
principles.example: Close all browser tabs except the document you are writing; place your phone in another room during focus blocks to remove the distraction cue entirely.
